physical.title: drawing
physical.summary: Charcoal drawing on machine-made paper, showing a woman seated on a cane-back chair and reading a book. To the side are two sketches of a little boy, dressed only in a T-shirt, amusing himself and a sketch of the head of the same child. The woman is wearing a traditional Vietnamese 'ao dai', a long side-fastening gown with slits up either side seam to the hips, over loose trousers and with flat sandals. Her hair is tied in a loose chignon at the nape of her neck after the fashion of married women. Signed, dated and inscribed.

cultural.vision_reason: A gouache propaganda-style painting of a Vietnamese mother in a dark green áo dài and headscarf holding a bundled baby, with a steel factory backdrop and Vietnamese slogan text ("the forest mountains are yours, the factory is also yours"); this is a mid-20th-century Vietnamese painting made within the culture, showing traditional dress and daily/political life.

reattribution.reason: This is a mid-20th-century propaganda-style poster painting showing a mother in ethnic minority dress with her child before a Vietnamese steel factory, a modern political artwork depicting Vietnamese life (likely a Northern minority woman rather than Kinh, but painted within Vietnamese national culture); it is a contemporary painted composition, not archaeological or traditional court art.

physical.title: painting
physical.summary: Poster-paint and chalk under-drawing painting on machine-made paper. This poster depicts a mother resting her baby on her hip with a factory in the background. She is dressed in the costume of a peasant with headdress, jade bangle, green "ao dai" (traditional dress) and belt, typical of the minority people of the North in Thai Nguyen. This is probably the Thai Nguyen steel factory, the heart of Vietnam's heavy industry at War. Her child is plump, healthy, happy and bundled in the warm brightly coloured clothes of the minority costume tradition. Signed, dated and inscribed (in the mother's voice) with words from a famous Vietnamese poem.

cultural.vision_reason: A hand-coloured Vietnamese propaganda-satirical print showing a woman in ao dai selling imported goods to reluctant customers — a modern Kinh political cartoon/print, clearly matching the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: satirical print
physical.summary: Propaganda-satirical relief-print, made of black ink and hand-coloured with fibre-tipped pen on shell-coated hand-made paper. It shows two customers refusing to buy foreign goods from a seductive young female shop vendor, who is leaning across the counter dressed in an 'ao dai' over white trousers and high heels. The vendor's emporium offers tempting imported commodities: 'ruoi mui' (liquor), 'keo tag' (sweets), 'xiga' (cigars), 'thuoc la' (cigarettes), 'biscuit' (biscuits), 'cacao' (chocolate) and 'do hop' (preserved or canned food). Signed with an unidentified seal mark and the letters "Khu", and inscribed.
